title: Runtime advertisement and version allocation schema for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need an API schema to publish a model's runtime advertisement surface that combines capability descriptors, allocatable version affinity, and resource budgeting hints. This schema will power model onboarding (what features a model supports), version pinning recommendations (which versions to prefer under different SLAs), and performance profile publishing (limits, context windows, and runtime hints).

Goals:
- Provide a single lightweight endpoint for runtime to fetch model 'advert' metadata for routing and serving decisions.
- Expose stable fields for downstream consumers (router, console, autoscaler) while allowing vendor/model-specific optional hints.
- Include allocatable budget and affinity hints to enable smart version pinning without leaking internal telemetry.
- Support backward-compatible extension so existing clients ignore unknown fields.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope: schema for advertisement records and API semantics for publish/get; storage format; migration plan; integration points (router, console, onboarding UI).
- Non-goal: implementing per-tenant policy enforcement; this ticket defines the contract and minimal runtime integration tests.

Proposed endpoints:
- POST /v1/model-ads (auth: onboarding service) - publish or upsert advert record.
- GET /v1/model-ads/{model_id} - fetch latest advert for routing/publication.
- GET /v1/model-ads?capability=chat&region=eu - filtering for discovery in console.

Core schema fields (high-level):
- advert_id: string (stable publishing id)
- model_id: string (catalog id)
- version: string (semver-like, optional for unversioned models)
- supported_features: [string] (e.g., text-generation, chat, tool-calls)
- max_context_tokens: integer (recommended context limit for cost/latency predictions)
- token_throughput_estimate: string (e.g., \"low\"|\"medium\"|\"high\")
- soft_concurrency_budget: integer (concurrent request budget suggested for default routing)
- preferred_routing_affinity: [\"low-latency\",\"cost-optimized\",\"stable-affinity\"]
- compatibility_tags: [string] (e.g., \"llama2-compatible\",\"32k-truncation\")
- quantization_profiles: [string] (labels referencing quantization options)
- feature_flags: [string] (opt-in experimental features)
- telemetry_hint: string (opaque hint: e.g., \"trace-v0\" used by internal dashboards)
- publish_time: ISO8601 timestamp
- deprecation_notice: string (optional human-readable: deprecate-after date + reason)

Important design notes / tradeoffs:
- Exposure vs. privacy: advertise only surface-level telemetry hints; no raw latency histograms or customer PII. Detailed telemetry stays in the monitoring plane.
- Budgeting semantics: soft_concurrency_budget is advisory. The router will translate to actual slot counts per deployment. This avoids tight coupling between advert and autoscaler.
- Version allocation: when multiple advert records exist for the same model_id, the router uses version + affinity + budget hints to pick candidate variants. The schema includes a small 'score_hint' field to simplify initial greedy selection.

Backward compatibility & rollout:
- Start with a schema v1.0 that is max-forward-compatible: unknown fields are ignored by consumers.
- Deploy onboarding service that writes both existing manifest records and new advert records for a subset of models (canary).
- Router: read fallback to previous manifest endpoint if advert lookup 404s.
- Console: surface new fields in experimental toggle; UI shows recommended budget and compatibility tags only when present.

Storage and indexing:
- Persist advert records in model-metadata store (existing index used by catalog service).
- Index on model_id, supported_features, compatibility_tags to support discovery queries.

Telemetry and alerts:
- Emit \"advert.publish\" events with schema_version and size.
- Dashboard: discoverability count (models advertising budget), and router-miss rate (fallbacks to old manifest).

Migration checklist:
1) API implementation + schema validation + migrations to metadata store.
2) Onboarding service writes adverts for new models.
3) Router reads adverts with 30% canary traffic.
4) Console uses adverts in read-only mode while feature flagged.
5) Gradual rollout and deprecation plan for old manifest endpoints.

Open questions (decisions pending):
- Should we include an explicit 'cost_hint_per_1k_tokens' numeric field or keep cost advice out of advert? (Con: drift; Pro: helpful for routing)
- How to manage owner lifecycle for advert records (who can deprecate)?

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456789/Runtime+Advertisement+Schema
- Initial PR (schema + validation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894
- Onboarding checklist: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cExampleDriveLink/edit
- Example console draft: https://app.prototype.redwood/ui/model-advert
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/model-ads accepts v1 payload and persists to metadata store
GET /v1/model-ads/{model_id} returns latest advert or 404 if absent
Router can fetch advert and fall back to manifest if advert missing
Schema versioning strategy documented in Confluence and linked in PR
Console shows advertised budget and compatibility tags behind feature flag
